questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A team routes conversations to staff when a message sounds upset or when the model rates its own confidence below 70. Most such routings turn out to be simple, while cases outside the written guidelines are settled by the agent at confidence above 90. Which change fits best?

options.text: Lower the cutoff to 50 and add more mood keywords to the detector
options.says: Ruled out because the guide calls these signals "unreliable proxies for actual case complexity".

options.text: Ask the model to score each case's difficulty from 1 to 10 and escalate the top ones
options.says: Ruled out because "A confidence number that the model writes about itself carries its blind spots".

options.text: Escalate on a request for a person, a gap in the policy or stalled work, with examples
options.says: The triggers are properties of the case, and examples carry the judgement.

options.text: Escalate any conversation that runs past six turns, whatever its content
options.says: Ruled out because "Complexity alone is not a trigger".

origin.section: When to escalate, and when not to

questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. A customer writes in capitals that the third late parcel is unacceptable and asks for nothing else. A reship is within the agent's tools. What should the agent do?

options.text: Escalate at once, because an upset customer wants a person
options.says: Ruled out because "Mood tells you how to speak and says little about what the case needs".

options.text: Acknowledge the anger and offer to fix the problem itself
options.says: An upset customer with a problem inside the agent's reach is helped, with the frustration acknowledged.

options.text: Ask the customer whether they would prefer to speak to a person
options.says: Ruled out because the agent "does not turn a complaint into one" (a request for a person).

options.text: Send the replacement quietly without mentioning the complaint
options.says: Ruled out because "the agent acknowledges the frustration, offers to resolve the issue", and a silent fix does not.

origin.section: Two signals that are not triggers

questions.stem: Scenario S1, customer support resolution agent. For the second time, the tool that reads a customer's order times out, and the customer is still waiting. What should happen?

options.text: Keep retrying quietly in the background until the tool finally answers
options.says: Ruled out because "A loop that carries on is the same failure that module 45 bounded in the agent loop".

options.text: Tell the customer to come back later and then close the chat politely
options.says: Ruled out because "the agent stops and hands off with what it tried", not with a request to come back.

options.text: Answer from the customer's earlier orders, which are probably similar to this one
options.says: Ruled out because a guess from earlier orders "is a guess that succeeds often enough to go unnoticed until it fails".

options.text: Stop at the attempt limit and hand over a short account of what was tried
options.says: Two attempts without progress hit the third trigger, and the hand-off carries what was tried.
